analyst_view.overall: Early view: Liverpool won 3-1 at Crystal Palace before the break, but their home form is poor, with five points from their Anfield games, and Dominik Szoboszlai is having tests on a knee problem. Manchester United are 18th after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, and reports say the club will decide Michael Carrick's future during the break, so United could arrive with a new manager. Carlos Baleba is out for a considerable period.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean higher: United's last two games finished 3-2 against Roma and 4-4 against Villa, and Liverpool scored three at Palace through Mac Allister, Wirtz and Isak. Liverpool have also been vulnerable at Anfield, losing 3-0 to City there.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. Liverpool should have more of the ball, but United's recent games have been end-to-end rather than long sieges, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards, with United expected to take 3.6. The rivalry adds edge and Liverpool had four players booked at Palace, but United had only one booking in the 4-4 with Villa. The two pull against each other, so I stay with the numbers.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, a high figure. Both teams' recent games have been open, which supports it, but a possible change of manager at United could make them more cautious at Anfield. I stay with the site for now.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: United have scored seven and conceded six in their last two games, and Liverpool's front players are in form. Both defences look easier to hit than the numbers assume.
